# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.

completion:
Collect and analyze data from continuous emissions monitoring systems (CEMS), if available. 
3. Verify sensor calibrations and validation processes.
4. Identify regulatory thresholds for the specific pollutants in question.
5. Document the frequency and duration of emissions exceeding regulatory limits.
6. Compare emissions data with permitted levels.
7. Measure meteorological conditions at the time of excessive emissions for context.
8. Assess additional data from stack emissions tests, dispersion modeling, or mobile monitoring if necessary.
9. Collect photographic evidence if possible.
10. Compile operational logs and maintenance activities, noting any correlation with spikes in emissions.
11. Review incident reports or complaints related to emissions.
12. Note any specific facility processes or activities occurring during times of excessive emissions.
13. Identify the pollutants being emitted (e.g., particulate matter, NOx, SO2, VOCs) and their concentrations.
